citations.quote: **(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it. **(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration: - **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$. - **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$. - **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$. The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption. **(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with $$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$ jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class: in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family); in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$. In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii). **(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced. **(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar $$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$ and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity $$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$ which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency. **(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family $$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$ and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family $$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$ The dimensionless numbers $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ are read as angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7. **(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

Define the *transition amplitude* $$A_{b_0a_0}(t,s):=e^{iE_{b_0}(t-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\bigr\rangle.$$ Then $$A_{b_0a_0}(t,s)=\delta_{a_0b_0}-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^te^{i(E_{b_0}-E_{a_0})(r-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle V(r)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\bigr\rangle\,dr+R_{b_0a_0}(t,s),$$ where the remainder satisfies the explicit bound $$|R_{b_0a_0}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^2}{2}.$$ Consequently, if $\eta:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ is integrable with $\|V(t)-V_0(t)\|\le\eta(t)$ for a family $V_0$ of self-adjoint bounded operators, assume the selected scalar coefficient $c_0(r)=\langle V_0(r)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\rangle$ is Lebesgue measurable (equivalently here, require it to be integrable). Then the first-order amplitude computed with $V_0$ differs from the exact one by at most $\frac1\hbar\int_s^t\eta(r)\,dr+e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2/2$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced. **(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar $$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$ and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity $$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$ which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency. **(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family $$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$ and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family $$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$ The dimensionless numbers $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ are read as angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7. **(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v:=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and adopt the interaction-picture readings of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]]: $E(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, $V_{I}(t)=E(-t)V(t)E(t)$, $U_{I}(t,s)=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator constructed by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. Then: (a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* $U$ is the unique family of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$, jointly strongly continuous on $I\times I$, with $U(s,s)=I$, $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, satisfying the vectorwise mild Schroedinger identity $$U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}E(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H,\ s,t\in I);$$ so the model's clause (c)(ii) declaration has exactly one solution. For $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_{0})$ the scalar curve $t\mapsto\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with $$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl[\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_{0}\varphi\bigr\rangle+\bigl\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle\Bigr].$$ No invariance of $D(H_{0})$ under $U$, no strong full Schroedinger equation for its domain vectors, and no operator-norm differentiability of $U$ with respect to the unbounded generator are asserted. (b) *Interaction picture.* For every $s,t\in I$ and every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$ the interaction state $\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)U(t,s)\psi(s)$ satisfies $\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi_{I}(t)=V_{I}(t)\psi_{I}(t)$; the interaction propagator is unitary with the cocycle and $U_{I}(t,s)^{*}=U_{I}(s,t)$, and its strong truncation bound is $\|U_{I}(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}D_{n}(t,s)\|\le e^{K(t-s)}(K(t-s))^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ for $s\le t$ with $K=v/\hbar$. (c) *Equivalence of the two readings.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$, every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ with $A$ bounded, every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the Schroedinger reading and the interaction reading give the same outcome probability: $$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B),\qquad A_{I}(t)=E(-t)AE(t),\quad \rho_{I}(t)=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$ and for pure preparations $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|$. For eigenvectors $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}$ of $H_{0}$ as in clause (e) of the model, the transition probabilities of the two pictures agree, $$p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}.$$ (d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded-control class; the mild identity, not a strong equation on $D(H_{0})$, is the evolution equation it establishes, and it asserts nothing about unbounded controls, invariant domains, measurement records, detectors, rates or empirical data.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be any complex Hilbert space, let $H_0=H_0^*$ have its exact dense domain $D(H_0)$, let $\hbar>0$, let $I=[a,b]$, and let $V:I\to\mathcal B(H)$ be strongly continuous with each $V(t)$ self-adjoint and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$. Put $K=v/\hbar$ and $$E(t)=e^{-itH_0/\hbar},\qquad V_I(t)=E(-t)V(t)E(t),\qquad B(t)=-iV_I(t)/\hbar.$$ The autonomous group is the CC arbitrary-H construction in [F1]. Then $V_I$ is strongly continuous, self-adjoint, and $\|V_I(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. For $s\le t$, define bounded operators by **vector strong integrals**: $$D_n(t,s)\psi=(-i/\hbar)^n\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V_I(t_n)\cdots V_I(t_1)\psi\,dt_1\cdots dt_n,\qquad D_0(t,s)=I.$$ For every fixed vector, these are integrals of continuous $H$-valued functions on a compact simplex (equivalently iterated integrals). They define a bounded operator by their action on vectors. This is the meaning of a strong operator integral; no norm-Bochner integrability into the Banach space $\mathcal B(H)$ is asserted. The series $U_I(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}D_n(t,s)$ converges in operator norm uniformly on the time triangle, with $$\|D_n(t,s)\|\le\frac{(K(t-s))^n}{n!},\qquad \left\|U_I(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^ND_n(t,s)\right\|\le e^{K(t-s)}\frac{(K(t-s))^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$ It extends to all $s,t\in I$ as a strongly continuous unitary evolution, with genuine inverse $U_I(s,t)=U_I(t,s)^{-1}=U_I(t,s)^*$ and full cocycle. For every $\psi\in H$ its first-endpoint map is $C^1$ in $H$, with $$U_I(t,s)\psi=\psi+\int_s^tB(r)U_I(r,s)\psi\,dr,\qquad \partial_tU_I(t,s)\psi=B(t)U_I(t,s)\psi.$$ The second endpoint satisfies $\partial_sU_I(t,s)\psi=-U_I(t,s)B(s)\psi$. These derivatives are strong derivatives; operator-norm differentiability is not claimed. The physical propagator $U(t,s)=E(t)U_I(t,s)E(-s)$ is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, has the full cocycle and inverse, and satisfies the vectorwise mild identity $$U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr.$$ For $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_0)$ the scalar curve is continuously differentiable, with $$\frac{d}{dt}\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\left[\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_0\varphi\rangle+\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle\right].$$ The proof actually permits arbitrary initial $\psi\in H$ in this weak equation. The original statement on $D(H_0)$ is therefore preserved. No invariance of $D(H_0)$ under the physical $U$, and no strong full Schrödinger derivative for its domain vectors, is deduced from these mere strong-continuity hypotheses. In particular, differentiating $E(t)U_I(t,s)E(-s)\psi$ by an unbounded product rule would require domain membership which has not been established.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of its clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of clause (c)(ii) constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. The readings of P1 and P2 are those of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; all times lie in $I$ and are read in seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). **(b) The free-flow factor.** The **free-flow factor** of the model is the autonomous flow of the unperturbed part, $$E(t):=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$ the reading of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] applied to the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$; it is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on all real arguments. This auxiliary group supplies $E(-t)$ and $E(t-s)$ even when those arguments lie outside $I$; the physical driven evaluation times $s,t$ remain in $I$. The **interaction-picture control** is the family $V_{I}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$, $$V_{I}(t):=E(-t)V(t)E(t),$$ which is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. The **interaction propagator** is $$U_{I}(t,s):=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)\qquad(s,t\in I),$$ and the model's clause (c)(ii) supplies, as the cited theorem proves, the decomposition $$U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s).$$ The interaction propagator is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, satisfies $U_{I}(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U_{I}(t,r)=U_{I}(t,s)U_{I}(s,r)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with $$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H),$$ all as supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; these are readings of that theorem in the model's vocabulary, not new assumptions. **(c) Interaction states and preparations.** For a Schroedinger-picture state vector $\psi(t)=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ the **interaction-picture state** is $$\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)\psi(t),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s),$$ and for a preparation $\rho$ with $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ the **interaction-picture preparation** is $$\rho_{I}(t):=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$ which is again a preparation of the model by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; for a pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$, $[\psi_{I}(t)]$ is pure. The map $\psi(t)\mapsto\psi_{I}(t)$ is unitary at every $t$, so $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|$. **(d) The two pictures assign the same outcome laws.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded and let $A_{I}(t):=E(-t)AE(t)$ be its interaction-picture representative, which is again a bounded self-adjoint observable with $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ for every Borel set $B$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint $T=-H_{0}/\hbar$. Then for every preparation $\rho$ specified at $s$ and every $t\in I$, $$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$ because $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)\bigr)$ by cyclicity of the trace; equivalently, for a pure preparation, $\|E_{A}(B)\psi(t)\|=\|E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)\psi_{I}(t)\|$. This identity is the precise sense in which the two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; it is a reading of P2 together with the cited mathematics, not a claim about apparatuses. **(e) Energy-basis transition amplitudes.** Let $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\in D(H_{0})$ be unit eigenvectors, $H_{0}\varphi_{a}=E_{a}\varphi_{a}$, $H_{0}\varphi_{b}=E_{b}\varphi_{b}$, and let $A_{ba}(t,s)$ and $p_{ba}(t,s)$ be the transition amplitude and probability of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]. Then $$A_{ba}(t,s)=e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle ,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$ by the decomposition of clause (b) and $E(-s)\varphi_{a}=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\varphi_{a}$, $\langle E(t)\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle=e^{-itE_{b}/\hbar}\langle\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle$; the phases are of modulus one ([[def-inner-product-space]]). The transition probability is therefore computable in either picture, and the definition records this as the reading used by the page's amplitude theorem; no measurement frequency or rate is defined. **(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are readings of the declared driven model, of clauses (b)-(e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], and of P1 and P2, in the vocabulary of the cited mathematics. The interaction picture is a change of description of the same model: it adds no assumption, no physical process, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about detectors, records or the laboratory realization of the model.

Let $H$ be a real or complex inner-product space ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), with inner product linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and with the induced length $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,vangle}$. The definitions below do not require completeness. When the term *Hilbert basis* is used, $H$ is additionally assumed complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]). **Orthonormal indexed family.** Let $I$ be any set. An indexed family $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of vectors of $H$ is **orthonormal** when $$\langle e_i,e_jangle=\delta_{ij}:= egin{cases}1,&i=j,\0,&i
e j,\end{cases} \qquad	ext{for all } i,j\in I .$$Because $1
e 0$ in the scalar field, the family contains no zero vector: $\|e_i\|^2=\langle e_i,e_iangle=1$, so $\|e_i\|=1$ for every $i$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); and the index map is injective, since $e_i=e_j$ with $i
e j$ would give $0=\langle e_i,e_jangle=1$. Thus an orthonormal family is the same thing as an orthonormal set together with a labelling of it, and in the sequel no choice is hidden in passing between the two descriptions. **Orthonormal set.** A subset $S\subseteq H$ is **orthonormal** when every $s\in S$ has $\|s\|=1$ and $\langle s,tangle=0$ for all distinct $s,t\in S$. For such an $S$ the family $(e_s)_{s\in S}$ with $e_s:=s$ is orthonormal in the indexed sense, and the image of an orthonormal indexed family is an orthonormal set. Orthogonal means $\langle s,tangle=0$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). **Independence and unique coefficients.** Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be orthonormal, let $F\subseteq I$ be finite, and let scalars $c_i$ satisfy $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=0$. For each fixed $j\in F$, linearity in the first argument gives$$0=\Bigl\langle \sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i,\;e_j\Bigrangle=\sum_{i\in F}c_i\langle e_i,e_jangle=c_j ,$$ so every finite subfamily of an orthonormal family is linearly independent. In particular the coefficients in a finite expansion are unique: if $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=\sum_{i\in F}d_ie_i$, then applying the computation to $c-d$ gives $c_i=d_i$ for every $i\in F$. **Closed linear span and completeness.** The **span** of an indexed family is the set of all finite linear combinations $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i$ with $F\subseteq I$ finite and scalars $c_i$; it is the smallest linear subspace of $H$ containing every $e_i$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). Its closure in the induced norm is the **closed linear span** of the family, the smallest closed linear subspace of $H$ containing every $e_i$. The family is **complete**, or is a **complete orthonormal system**, when its closed linear span is all of $H$. A **Hilbert basis**, or **orthonormal basis**, of $H$ is a complete orthonormal family in $H$. **The empty family.** The span of the empty family is $\{0\}$, which is already closed, so the empty family is complete exactly when $H=\{0\}$. Thus the zero Hilbert space always has a Hilbert basis, namely the empty one. **Not a Hamel basis, and no order is assumed.** A Hilbert basis is a basis only in the sense of closed linear span: for an infinite-dimensional $H$ the vectors of $H$ are in general **not** finite linear combinations of a Hilbert basis, and the expansion of an arbitrary vector is a norm limit of finite partial sums, not a finite sum. No enumeration, ordering or countability of the index set is part of the definition; the partial sums are indexed by the finite subsets of $I$, ordered by inclusion, and that is the convention used on this page. **Coefficient notation.** For orthonormal $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $x\in H$ the scalars $\langle x,e_iangle$ are the **coefficients** of $x$ with respect to the family. They are well defined for every $x$, without any assumption that the family is complete.

Let $F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, with conjugation equal to the identity on $\mathbb R$ and with complex conjugation as in [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]. An **inner product** on an $F$-vector space $V$ is a function $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle:V\times V\to F$ such that for all $u,v,w\in V$ and $a,b\in F$: 1. $\langle au+bv,w\rangle=a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle$; 2. $\langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle}$; 3. $\langle v,v\rangle$ is real and nonnegative, and $\langle v,v\rangle=0$ if and only if $v=0$. The first two clauses imply conjugate-linearity in the second argument: $\langle u,av+bw\rangle=\overline a\langle u,v\rangle+\overline b\langle u,w\rangle$. This is the linear-first convention of [[def-sesquilinear-and-hermitian-forms-over-a-field-with-involution]]. A vector space equipped with an inner product is an **inner product space**.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space, $$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$ Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field $\mathbb K$, read in the real case from [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from [[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]. A linear map $T:X\to Y$ ([[def-linear-map]]) is a **bounded linear operator** when there is a real constant $C \ge 0$ such that $$\|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \qquad \text{for all } x \in X.$$ Any such $C$ is called a **bound** for $T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let $T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The **operator norm** of $T$ is $$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$ The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]). In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice principle is used for this assertion. The same number is the least bound of $T$: $$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$ If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives $$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$ When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$, so $\|T\| = 0$.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition. **(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$ the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b). **(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2. **(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable. **(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation. **(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it. **(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it. **(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable. **(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$ By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here. **(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point. **(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (a)), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$, $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ by clause (b) of the same lemma. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3). **(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted. **(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**Density operators.** Let $H
e\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $ho$ with $\operatorname{tr}ho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted $$D(H):=\{ho:ho\ 	ext{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$ An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here. **Pure states.** A state $ho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with $$ho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,uangle u\quad(x\in H),$$ where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map $$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)},$$ on the ray space $R(H)$, with $
u$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is $$\widehatho(\psi):= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$ which equals $T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)}$; thus $\widehatho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray. **Purity.** For $ho\in D(H)$ the operator $ho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langleho^{2}x,xangle=\langleho x,ho xangle\ge0$, and trace class because $ho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $ho$ is the real number $$\mathcal P(ho):=\operatorname{tr}(ho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$ The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only. **Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Z^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature. **(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. **(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$; the vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is experimentally determined and $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$. These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]]. **(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities. 1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless. 2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure. 3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$. 4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. 5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux. 6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them. 7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention. 8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list. **(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below. **(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it. **(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$. **(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$. **(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here. **(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page. **(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

derivations.claim: [Exact pair amplitude without completeness] The interaction-picture supplier in [F2] gives $U=E(t)U_IE(-s)$ and $U_I=I+D_1+T_2$ with $D_1\xi=-(i/\hbar)\int_s^tV_I(r)\xi\,dr$ and $\|T_2\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2/2$. For the two specified eigenvectors, $\langle E(t)x,\varphi_j\rangle=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}\langle x,\varphi_j\rangle$ and $E(-s)\varphi_i=e^{iE_is/\hbar}\varphi_i$, so the correct model amplitude is $A_{ji}=e^{i(E_i-E_j)s/\hbar}\langle U_I\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$. Its zeroth term is $\delta_{ij}$. Also $\langle V_I(r)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle=e^{i(E_j-E_i)r/\hbar}\langle V(r)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$. Passing this continuous bounded linear pairing through the vector integral gives exactly $A^{(1)}_{ji}$ and $R_{ji}=e^{i(E_i-E_j)s/\hbar}\langle T_2\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$, with the advertised remainder by [F3]. Only the fixed pair was used; a complete eigenfamily is unnecessary. For the selected integrable coefficient of $V_0$, subtracting the two first-order scalar integrals and using $|\langle(V-V_0)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle|\le\eta$ proves the stated $\hbar^{-1}\int_s^t\eta$ bound. This proves (a), including free, zero-time and diagonal cases. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

[Sinusoidal evaluation] With $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and $u:=r-s$, $\omega r+\vartheta=\omega u+\vartheta_{0}$, so $\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)=\frac{1}{2}(e^{i(\omega u+\vartheta_{0})}+e^{-i(\omega u+\vartheta_{0})})$ and $$A^{(1)}_{ji}=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\Bigl[e^{i\vartheta_{0}}\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{i(\Delta+\hbar\omega)u/\hbar}du+e^{-i\vartheta_{0}}\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{i(\Delta-\hbar\omega)u/\hbar}du\Bigr],$$ the two integrals being $\tau$ when their frequency vanishes and $(e^{i\theta\tau/\hbar}-1)/(i\theta/\hbar)$ otherwise; this is the displayed decomposition with $a_{\pm}$ and the stated convention. For $a_{+}$, $|e^{i\theta\tau/\hbar}-1|=2|\sin(\theta\tau/(2\hbar))|$ and the modulus of the quotient by $i\theta/\hbar$ is $2\hbar|\sin(\theta\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\theta|$ for $\theta=\Delta-\hbar\omega\ne0$, giving $|a_{+}|=|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle||\sin((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\Delta-\hbar\omega|$; at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$ the quotient is $\tau$ and the same modulus formula gives the limit $|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|\tau/(2\hbar)$. For $a_{-}$ the same computation gives $|a_{-}|=|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle||\sin((\Delta+\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|\le|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$. This is clause (b). [F1, F3, algebra]

[Probability error for transition and survival] By [F2], $p_{ji}=|A_{ji}|^2$, and step 1.1 gives $A_{ji}=b_{ji}+R$, where $b_{ji}=\delta_{ij}+A^{(1)}$ and $|R|\le\varepsilon$. The identity $|b+R|^2-|b|^2=2\operatorname{Re}(R\overline b)+|R|^2$ therefore gives $|p_{ji}-|b_{ji}|^2|\le2|b_{ji}|\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2$. For $i\ne j$, $b_{ji}=A^{(1)}$, giving the displayed transition bound; for $i=j$, $b_{ii}=1+A^{(1)}$ and $|b_{ii}|\le1+|A^{(1)}|$, giving the displayed survival bound. No diagonal term is dropped. This proves (c). [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

[Scope] Only the bounded control, the fixed eigenpair, finite times and the choice hypotheses entered; the remainder grows like $e^{K\tau}\tau^{2}$ and no infinite-time limit, density of states, rate or decay was formed, which is clause (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given] ∎
